MINE 1024.title: Leadership and Service in the Mineral Industries
MINE 1024.description: Leadership and service principles. Awareness of self and others through personality typing. Strategic planning. Importance of energy and mineral industries to developed and developing countries as well as associated consequences. Mineral extraction and purification processes and calculations. Conflict resolution. Challenges and opportunities available in the energy and mineral industries. May include guest speakers and field trips.

MINE 1034.title: Automation and Data Analytics in the Mineral Industries
MINE 1034.description: Discovering challenges and opportunities available in autonomous vehicles, systems, and data analytics associated with the energy and mineral industries. Fundamentals of robotics and data analytics; hands on projects with autonomous kits and drones; analysis of industry data, including production studies; introduction to presentation of complex data in a simplified manner; introduction to simulations and digital twins.

MINE 1044.title: Space Mining
MINE 1044.description: Explore challenges and opportunities in off-earth mining. Resources currently identified on earth and critical uses; astroidal, lunar, and martian resources; operating conditions in space; environmental, social, and governance issues; economic drivers; in situ resource utilization.

MINE 2114.title: Energy and Raw Materials: Geopolitics and Sustainable Development
MINE 2114.description: Supply and demand of energy resources and raw materials. Domestic and global trends. Development of energy and mineral resources. Electricity generation, efficiency, and distribution. Energy and raw materials infrastructure Disparities in resource-producing vs. resource-consuming regions. Environmental considerations and engineering management. Land use and reclamation. Greenhouse gas management. Policy, regulations, and incentives. Geopolitical considerations. Conservation and efficiency. Sustainable development. This course is available to undergraduate students of all ranks and all majors.

MINE 2504.title: Introduction to Mining Engineering
MINE 2504.description: Introduction to the complete field of mining and minerals engineering, including phases of mine development, discreet mining methods and mineral processing operations. Consideration in unconventional oil and gas development. Emphasis on basic engineering problem solving skills, and considerations for worker health and safety, economics, and environmental and social issues.

MINE 2534.title: Mine Surveying and Mapping
MINE 2534.description: Specialized principles of field surveying and mapping as applied to the delineation of mineral deposits and the design and monitoring of surface and underground mining operations. Introduction to modern surveying instruments, field techniques, and computational procedures. Basic digital mine mapping to include standard mine symbols and representation of surface and underground mine workings. Partially duplicates ENGE 2824.

MINE 2544.title: Leadership for Responsible Mining
MINE 2544.description: Principles of leadership for the global resource industries including identification of project impacts and risks, stakeholder analysis and conflict management. Emphasis on engineering ethics and effective communications. Sustainable development of mineral and energy resources, with focus on emerging technical, economic, environmental and social issues in the US and abroad.

MINE 2564.title: Resource Exploration and Design
MINE 2564.description: Basic methods and concepts in exploration and modeling of ore bodies. Resource exploration planning. Exploration technologies for potential mine sites. Design of mining systems. Computational modeling of ore bodies and mine systems. Environmental, regulatory, ethical, and social considerations in mine system design.

MINE 3544.title: Mineral Processing Laboratory
MINE 3544.description: Laboratory investigations of the unit operations and principles of mineral processing including ore preparation (size reduction, mineral liberation, and classification) and mineral recovery (froth flotation, electrostatic separation, magnetic separation, and solid-liquid separation).

MINE 3564.title: Underground Mine Design
MINE 3564.description: Design fundamentals of mining systems and stope development for tabular and massive underground mineral deposits. Equipment selection and application, permitting, cost analysis and production simulation.

MINE 3574.title: Surface Mine and Quarry Design
MINE 3574.description: Surface mining methods, and their selection; mine planning and design; excavation, haulage and ancillary systems; equipment selection and maintenance; impoundment and piles design; mine closure/reclamation.

MINE 3584.title: Ventilation Engineering
MINE 3584.description: Subsurface ventilation systems. Ventilation planning and design, laws of airflow, airway resistance. Ventilation surveys, network analysis, ventilation economics. Ventilation software. Fan types, impeller theory, fan laws and testing. Mine ventilation thermodynamics.

MINE 3604.title: Mining Geomechanics
MINE 3604.description: Properties and behavior of geologic materials and masses and their classifications and ratings. Design principles of structures founded on and in rocks and basic aspects of ground control in mining. Laboratory techniques used in the determination of geologic materials properties and behavior. Determination of rock index properties, strengths, failure criterion and mechanical behavior.

MINE 3624.title: Mineral Resource Project Management
MINE 3624.description: Applied and theoretical concepts in the valuation and management of mining and energy extraction projects. Project engineering, resource management, scheduling, and tracking. Estimation of capital costs, operating costs, and revenues for underground and surface mines, mineral beneficiation plants, and oil and gas ventures. Commodity sales contracts and price projections. Cash flow analysis, revenue-generating and service producing alternative selection, taxes/deductions. Quantitative risk analysis including stochastic simulation. Environmental, ethical, and legal considerations in project management.

MINE 3634.title: Fundamentals of Mineral Processing
MINE 3634.description: Principles of mineral processing with an emphasis on metallurgical data evaluation, unit operations, and flowsheet configurations. Metallurgical accounting, slurry calculations, grade-recovery relationships, chemical aspects of mineral processing, and particle size analysis. Unit operations including rushing, grinding, size separation, gravity separation, magnetic and electrostatic separation, froth dewatering. Laboratory investigations of the unit operations and principles of mineral processing.

MINE 3644.title: Applications in Mineral Processing
MINE 3644.description: Applied concepts in the design and operation of mineral processing plants. Flowsheet engineering, unit selection, unit sizing, water/mass flow balancing, simulation, process control, and cost estimation. Environmental, economic, and legal considerations in process plant design.

MINE 3664.title: Fluids and Thermodynamics for Resources
MINE 3664.description: Fluid properties and hydrostatics. Derivation and application of the continuity, momentum, and energy equation (Bernoulli's equation) for ideal and real fluid flow (laminar or turbulent). Properties of pure substances: property tables, property software, equations of state. First law of thermodynamics. Second law of thermodynamics. Gas mixtures. Applications in the resource extraction industries.

MINE 3674.title: Explosives and Rock Fragmentation
MINE 3674.description: Rock fragmentation for excavation; drilling fragmentation, rock drilling systems; blasting fragmentation, types and properties of commercial explosives and accessories, system of initiation, design of blasting rounds, applications in mining and construction, structural damage criteria, overbreak control, safe practice and regulations; fragmentation by excavation machines; excavation system selection and design.

MINE 3714.title: Petroleum and Natural Gas Reservoir Engineering
MINE 3714.description: Introduction to oil and gas reservoirs; basics of reservoir rock and fluid properties; fundamentals of different petroleum reservoirs; determination of oil and gas in place; material balance equation; prediction of transient pressure distribution; prediction of saturation distribution; basics of recovery mechanisms; single and multiphase flows in petroleum reservoirs; and prediction of recovery factor and production rate.

MINE 4614.title: Health and Safety Systems
MINE 4614.description: Investigation of health and safety management systems. Study of mine legislation; data analysis of accidents; hazard identification; risk management; training programs; emergency response plans.

MINE 4624.title: Mine and Water Reservoir Engineering
MINE 4624.description: Essential topics related to water in resource extraction projects, including surface and ground water hydrology, chemistry and treatment of mine-influenced waters and waters from unconventional oil and gas production, and mine dewatering. Emphasis on basic design calculations and modeling.

MINE 4635.title: Mining Engineering Capstone
MINE 4635.description: 4635: Serves as the capstone design course sequence for Mining and Minerals Engineering. Undertake a comprehensive design project and feasibility study that integrates courses taken throughout their curriculum, in consideration of public and occupational health, safety, and welfare, as well as global, cultural, social, environmental, and economic factors and constraints. Includes exploration of professional and ethical obligations of engineers and impacts of projects on communities, project management, communication, and working in teams. 4636: Serves as the capstone design course sequence for Mining and Minerals Engineering. Undertake a comprehensive design project and feasibility study that integrates courses taken throughout their curriculum, in consideration of public and occupational health, safety, and welfare, as well as global, cultural, social, environmental, and economic factors and constraints. Includes exploration of professional and ethical obligations of engineers and impacts of projects on communities, project management, communication, and working in teams. Culminates in the preparation of a technical report that describes the commercial development, extraction and closure of a mineral deposit under global reporting standards, and provides detailed operational layouts, production calculations, and engineering cost analyses.
MINE 4635.prereq: MINE 2544 and (MINE 3564 or MINE 3574) and MINE 3624

MINE 4636.title: Mining Engineering Capstone

Undertake a comprehensive design project and feasibility study that integrates courses taken throughout their curriculum, in consideration of public and occupational health, safety, and welfare, as well as global, cultural, social, environmental, and economic factors and constraints. Includes exploration of professional and ethical obligations of engineers and impacts of projects on communities, project management, communication, and working in teams. Culminates in the preparation of a technical report that describes the commercial development, extraction and closure of a mineral deposit under global reporting standards, and provides detailed operational layouts, production calculations, and engineering cost analyses.

MINE 4644.title: Environmental Management for Mining and Geoenergy
MINE 4644.description: Environmental impacts of mines and geoenergy resource development projects, including water, land and air pollution. Statutory and regulatory environmental requirements, with an emphasis on permitting, monitoring and compliance. Best practices for environmental management systems.

MINE 4654.title: Mine Power Systems and Automation
MINE 4654.description: Fundamentals of electrical theory. Circuit elements, calculations and network analysis. Components and design of mine power systems. Motors, cables, load flow analyses, transmission and distribution. Electrical safety. U.S. mine-specific regulation, intrinsic safety and permissibility. Applications in mine systems automation via programmable logic control. Basic ladder logic routines.

MINE 4664.title: Resource Engineering Leadership Seminar
MINE 4664.description: Invited speakers and subject experts, assigned readings, facilitated activities and discussions, personality and values assessment, learning taxonomy and learning styles, diversity in the workplace, implications of personal differences for workplace and leadership dynamics, strategies and best practices for effective leadership, oral and written communication for diverse audiences. Pre: Senior Standing.

MINE 4744.title: Computer Programming and Data Analyses for Mining Engineering
MINE 4744.description: This problem-solving-oriented course introduces senior mining engineering students to applied programming using multiple programming languages (PLs) for mathematical modeling and data analysis. The course emphasizes developing mathematical solutions, numerical modeling, and simulation of mining and mineral processing systems, as well as data-driven approaches focused on data analysis and machine learning methods relevant to mining engineering. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to integrate computational and data-analytic tools into engineering practice. Pre: Senior Standing

MINE 5025.title: Advanced Mining Design
MINE 5025.description: Selected advanced design problems in mining including roof control, shafts, material handling, transportation, drainage, and ventilation. Advanced work in creative quantitative design or ore milling and coal preparation plants.

MINE 5045.title: Advanced Mineral Processing
MINE 5045.description: The theory of reactions in flotation systems and application of physical chemistry to mineral beneficiation. Advanced studies in electrostatic and magnetic separation. Theory and application of differential gravity separations. Advanced studies in comminution, grinding systems, and coal preparation plant design, simulation, and control.

MINE 5114.title: Sustainable Development of Mineral and Energy Resources
MINE 5114.description: Sustainable development in the context of mineral and energy resource extraction, including evolution and current status of principles, challenges, and best practices relative to various industry sectors and global regions; criteria for compatible engineering designs; and management strategies for stakeholder engagement and social license to operate. Pre: Graduate standing.

MINE 5214.title: Multicomponent Thermodynamics
MINE 5214.description: Phase behavior of petroleum fluids; saturation pressure calculations; fluid phase equilibria; first and second law of thermodynamics for open systems; two-phase fluid properties; production engineering and separator calculation; and the applications to gas injection enhanced oil recovery and carbon dioxide sequestration in petroleum reservoirs. Pre: Graduate standing.

MINE 5234.title: Numerical Modeling of Petroleum Reservoirs
MINE 5234.description: Introduction to oil and gas reservoirs; basic Darcy-scale fluid mechanics in petroleum reservoirs; numerical solution of partial differential equations on the basis of finite difference methods; 1D, 2D, and 3D single-/two-phase flow simulations; transient and boundary-value problems; global challenges associated with energy and water; and the applications to water flooding and hydrocarbon production in petroleum reservoirs. Pre: Graduate standing.

MINE 5324.title: Particulate Process Engineering
MINE 5324.description: Advanced studies in process engineering as applied to particulate separation techniques in mineral processing and coal preparation. Collection, reconciliation, and interpretation of plant performance data. Process modeling as it relates to analysis and optimization of unit operations. Elements of process design including circuit analysis and flowsheet calculations. Focus on industrial problems. Pre: Graduate standing.

MINE 5334.title: Hydrometallurgy
MINE 5334.description: Fundamental aspects of hydrometallurgy for the minerals industry, speciation and phase diagrams of aqueous or solid/aqueous reaction systems, thermodynamic and kinetic analyses of hydrometallurgical reactions, the principles and practices of diverse leaching techniques for metal extraction, solvent extraction for metal purification, and various other metal purification methods. Pre: Graduate standing.

MINE 5504.title: Mining Finance
MINE 5504.description: Advanced applications of resource project financing using case studies, emphasizing corporate decision making and investing related to resource exploration and development; asset valuation, discounted cash flow analysis, net present value, internal rate of return, and risk adjustment; emphasis on practical applications of financial modeling with sensitivity analyses. Pre: Graduate Standing.

MINE 5744.title: Computer programming and data analyses for mining engineering
MINE 5744.description: This problem-solving oriented course introduces senior mining engineering students to applied programming using both MATLAB and Python. MATLAB is emphasized as a tool for developing mathematical solutions, numerical modeling, and simulation of mining and mineral processing systems. Python is applied to data-driven approaches, with a focus on data analysis and machine learning methods relevant to mining engineering. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to integrate computational and data analytic tools into engineering practice.

MINE 5944.title: Seminar
MINE 5944.description: Two written or oral presentations to be made by all graduate students on their thesis topics; also participation in all other graduate student, visiting lecturer, and faculty member presentations during their scholastic tenure. Required of all students for graduation. All graduate students in the department are required to enroll in the seminar for two semesters and to attend all the seminars.
